inputs.share_count_basis: FY2026 AR note 24(c)(iii): 1,018.091m shares in issue at 31-Mar-2026 including 1.536m treasury shares, which were transferred in May 2026 to the share-award trust to vest awards (so counted as outstanding); plus 0.555m dilutive options from the note 10(b) diluted-EPS table = 1,018.6m. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: OCF 712.8 - capex 152.2 - lease rentals 119.9 (capital element 103.8 + interest element 16.1, both in financing). Unadjusted OCF-capex was 560.6. Interest received (23.6) is classified in INVESTING by Vitasoy, so it is not inside OCF and needs no further strip.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income 25.1 (segment note) is received in investing activities, outside reported OCF, so it is already excluded from the flow base; the cash that earns it (1,207.2) is in the bridge. Set to 0 here to avoid stripping it twice.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR cash-flow add-back 'Equity settled share-based payment expenses' 24.3m HKD; no net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes 0 all years). Share-award trust purchases (0 in FY26, 7.6 in FY25) are the cash mechanism for awards and are not added on top.
inputs.buyback_note: Discretionary buy-back programme: FY2025 40.6 (4.2m shares, March 2025), FY2026 419.8 (53.2m shares, 4.96% of opening shares), of which H1 FY2026 199.5. Partly funded by the VSL (Shanghai land and buildings) disposal. Not a stated recurring programme with a fixed quantum; treated as capital return. Value-neutral in this model because the count is held flat and SBC is expensed; the FY26 buybacks are already reflected in the lower share count and lower cash.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD flows; HKD pegged to USD so HKD risk-free ~3.5% (10y HKGB/UST), ERP 5.5%, beta ~0.85 for a consumer-staples beverage maker with ~53% Chinese Mainland revenue -> cost of equity ~8.2-8.7%. Net cash balance sheet, so WACC = CoE = 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk lives in the scenario flows and weights, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease rentals (principal 103.8 + interest 16.1 = 119.9, ~2.0% of revenue) deducted via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (221.9 at 31-Mar-2026) EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY26 total D&A 480.1 less ROU depreciation 113.7 = 366.3, 6.0% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are whole-group (100% consolidated); NCI (FY26 share of profit 7.1, ~2.5% of group NI) deducted once in the equity bridge at book value 108.3 (FY2026 balance sheet).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations. Vitasoy is an operating consumer-staples company (plant-milk and tea beverages, tofu) with no financial-services or property-trust character, so the routing table's 'operating company, non-US' row applies. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). FY0 is FY2026 (year to 31-Mar-2026). FY0 EBITDA anchor is UNDERLYING: parser EBITDA 910.0 (op profit + D&A) includes the 150.9 VSL disposal gain and the 97.7 VAP (Australia) PP&E impairment; ex those = 856.8, plus SBC 24.3 (engine deducts SBC separately) = 881.1 = 14.5% pre-SBC, pre-lease EBITDA margin. FY2025 on the same basis was ~14.5% (873.8 + 14.5 impairment + 21.8 SBC). Capex has run at only 2.0-2.5% of revenue FY23-26 versus D&A ex-ROU of ~6% -- the residue of the FY19-20 Dongguan/Wuhan plant build (capex 900-1,080m). Base case lets capex normalise to ~4% and D&A converge down to it by year 10; carrying FY26's low capex forward would overstate terminal FCF. Cash tax ramps from ~20% (FY26 cash tax paid 62.3 on ~350 underlying EBIT, sheltered by Mainland tax losses being utilised and the deferred-tax unwind) to 25% (blend of 25% PRC, 16.5% HK, 5% PRC dividend withholding, and Australian losses without tax shelter; reported effective rate 24-30% across FY19-26). Revenue is still below the FY2019/FY2021 peak (~7.5bn): Mainland China general-trade softness and price cuts drove FY26 -3%; H2 FY26 revenue (2,834) was flat on H2 FY25 (2,830) after H1 -6%, so momentum has stabilised. Equity bridge: NCI at book. JV investment (Philippines, URC) is small and its losses are already in reported earnings; not added.
inputs.data_quality_note: EBITDA for annual periods is parser-computed (operating profit + D&A); half-years company-reported. total_debt is bank loans only.

historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: OCF - capex - lease rentals (principal + interest) - SBC, HKD m. FY2022 lease rentals taken from FY2023 comparative (91.2).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case revenue path average (equity CAGR is negative because of buybacks and payouts exceeding earnings, EPS CAGRs are trough-distorted)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-4.3%) diverges from EPS 3yr (+82.9%, off the FY2023 trough of 0.043) and EPS 5yr (-12.6%). Neither is a usable forward rate: book value has shrunk through FY22 losses, dividends and the FY26 buyback, and EPS is recovering from the FY22-23 Mainland collapse. Selected rate is a judged revenue path.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (+28.6%) exceeds reported (+21.2%) only because FY2023's owner base was depressed by lease cash; SBC is small (0.3-0.4% of revenue) and not growing faster than cash flow. FY2026 owner FCF fell vs FY2025 on higher cash tax (62 vs 31) and a working-capital outflow; the FY24-26 average owner FCF is ~506.

base.narrative: Mainland stabilises (general trade flat, Omni/snack-chain channels grow), HK holds ~12% operating margin, ANZ moves from a 40m adjusted loss toward breakeven: margin recovers ~1.3pp to 15.8%, below the FY2019-21 pre-collapse 16.5-18%.

scenario_narratives.base: Chinese Mainland (53% of revenue) stops shrinking: general-trade sell-through stabilises, as H2 FY26 already suggests, and the Omni / snack-chain channel grows. HK Operation holds share and its ~12% margin with Macau fixed under new leadership; ANZ narrows its loss after the FY26 impairment and Singapore stays profitable. Group revenue grows 1.5% in FY27 and ~3% thereafter, EBITDA margin recovers to 15.8%, capex normalises from the post-build trough of ~2.5% to ~4% of revenue, and cash tax rises to 25% as Mainland losses are used up.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mainland returns to growth as VITA lemon tea and soymilk innovation regain share in general trade while Omni customisation scales; ANZ reaches breakeven via oat/protein and higher-margin coffee-shop and NZ channels; operating leverage on the under-utilised Dongguan/Wuhan capacity lifts EBITDA margin back to 17.5%, near the FY2019-21 level. Revenue compounds ~5% for five years and regains the FY2021 peak around year 4.
scenario_narratives.bear: Mainland plant-milk and RTD tea become a structural price war (domestic brands, private label in snack chains, Nongfu/ Master Kong tea promotion) and general trade keeps eroding; further price cuts and trade spend compress gross margin; ANZ stays loss-making and needs more impairment. Revenue falls 3% in FY27 and only creeps back at 1-1.5%, EBITDA margin settles at 13%, and terminal growth is 1.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: revenue has fallen five of the last seven years, the Mainland segment that drives it is mid price-competition and the FY22 boycott/collapse shows how fast it can swing. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs Mainland recovery, ANZ turnaround and margin restoration all at once. Base 50% reflects the stabilising H2 FY26 run-rate and a net-cash balance sheet that removes any solvency tail.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A net-cash, brand-led beverage franchise valued on owner FCF after lease rentals and SBC, with margins allowed to recover only part of the way to the pre-FY2022 peak and capex normalised up from its post-build trough. The question the price asks is whether the Chinese Mainland business is in cyclical or structural decline.
key_risks_to_valuation: Chinese Mainland price competition and general-trade channel erosion (53% of revenue)
Capex normalisation: FY23-26 capex of 2-2.5% of revenue is below maintenance; a return to plant-build spending would cut FCF
ANZ (Vitasoy Australia Products) remains loss-making after the AUD19m FY26 impairment
Cash tax rate rising as Mainland tax losses are used up
FY26 buyback funded partly by a one-off land disposal; capital return may not repeat
